answer: An agent marketplace allocates job access in proportion to escrowed stake, not account count, so splitting one deposit among a thousand identities creates no extra capacity. Viewed through this prism, a ripple of new accounts is harmless: to control 30% of access, an attacker must lock 30% of all stake. A fixed withdrawal delay keeps that capital tied up even at demand’s nadir, imposing financing costs for the duration of the attack.
